titleStmt.title: A Wearable IoT Device for Personal Safety Alerts

div.p: We present a wrist-worn device that raises an alert within 1.8 seconds of a triggered gesture. Field trials with 40 participants show a false-positive rate below 3 percent.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Personal safety wearables have proliferated over the last decade.
Existing systems trade latency for battery life; we target both.

div.head: Proposed System Architecture
div.p: The device pairs an accelerometer with a low-power cellular radio.
A gesture classifier runs on-device to avoid streaming raw sensor data.

div.head: Results and Evaluation
div.p: Mean alert latency was 1.8 seconds across 40 field trials in urban settings.

div.head: Limitations
div.p: The trial cohort skewed young and urban; rural coverage was not evaluated.

div.head: Future Work
div.p: We plan to evaluate fall detection as a secondary trigger.
